events.title: Cuneiform Emerges at Uruk
events.body: The world's earliest writing system develops from clay tokens used to record grain and livestock, becoming the first script for recording language and law.

events.title: Sargon Founds the Akkadian Empire
events.body: Sargon of Akkad unites the Sumerian city-states into history's first known multi-ethnic empire.

events.title: Hammurabi's Code Carved in Stone
events.body: Babylon's king publishes 282 laws on a black diorite stele, one of the earliest surviving law codes governing an entire society.

events.title: Nineveh Falls
events.body: A coalition of Babylonians and Medes sacks the Assyrian capital, ending centuries of Assyrian dominance over Mesopotamia.

events.title: Cyrus the Great Takes Babylon
events.body: The Persian king enters Babylon without a battle, absorbing Mesopotamia into the Achaemenid Empire and ending Babylonian independence.

events.title: Narmer Unites Upper and Lower Egypt
events.body: A single king, likely Narmer, unifies the Nile valley into one kingdom, founding one of the world's first territorial states.

events.title: The Old Kingdom Begins
events.body: The Third Dynasty ushers in Egypt's first great age of pyramid building and centralized rule from Memphis.

events.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza Is Completed
events.body: Pharaoh Khufu's tomb rises as the tallest structure on Earth, a record it will hold for nearly 4,000 years.

events.title: The Battle of Kadesh
events.body: Ramesses II fights the Hittites to a standstill in one of history's largest chariot battles, leading to one of the earliest known peace treaties.

events.title: Death of Cleopatra VII
events.body: Egypt's last active pharaoh dies after Rome's conquest, and the millennia-old kingdom becomes a Roman province.

events.title: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro Rise
events.body: Twin cities along the Indus River emerge with grid-planned streets, standardized brick sizes, and sophisticated drainage systems unmatched elsewhere in the Bronze Age world.

events.title: A Standardized Script Appears on Seals
events.body: Thousands of carved steatite seals bear a still-undeciphered script, used widely enough to suggest long-distance trade record-keeping.

events.title: Trade Networks Reach Mesopotamia
events.body: Indus merchants exchange carnelian beads, ivory, and cotton textiles with Sumerian city-states via sea routes through the Persian Gulf.

events.title: The Great Bath Falls Out of Use
events.body: Mohenjo-daro's massive public water tank, likely used for ritual bathing, is abandoned as the city's population begins to decline.

events.title: The Civilization Fades
events.body: Following climate shifts and the drying of the Sarasvati river system, Indus cities are gradually abandoned, their script falling silent for millennia.

events.title: The First Olympic Games
events.body: City-states pause their rivalries to compete at Olympia, founding a tradition of pan-Hellenic athletic competition that will run for over a thousand years.

events.title: Draco's Harsh Laws Are Written Down
events.body: Athens gets its first written law code, so severe that “draconian” will still describe harsh punishment millennia later.

events.title: Cleisthenes Founds Athenian Democracy
events.body: Reforms give ordinary male citizens a direct vote in the assembly, an experiment in self-rule without precedent in the ancient world.

events.title: Victory at Marathon
events.body: Athens repels the first Persian invasion at the Battle of Marathon, a triumph later commemorated by a runner's legendary sprint to deliver the news.

events.title: Rome Conquers Greece
events.body: After the sack of Corinth, Greece becomes a Roman province, even as Greek art, philosophy, and language go on to shape Roman civilization itself.

events.title: Legendary Founding of Rome
events.body: According to tradition, Romulus founds the city on the Palatine Hill, beginning a settlement that will grow into an empire spanning three continents.

events.title: The Roman Republic Is Established
events.body: Romans expel their last king and found a republic governed by elected magistrates and the Senate.

events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.body: Senators stab Caesar to death on the Ides of March, fearing his growing power — the act triggers the civil wars that end the Republic.

events.title: The Colosseum Opens
events.body: Emperor Titus inaugurates the Flavian Amphitheatre with 100 days of games, seating some 50,000 spectators.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.body: Germanic general Odoacer deposes the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus — an event later historians mark as Rome's end in the West.

name: Persia
summary: Persia was ruled by three successive empires: the Achaemenids, founded by Cyrus the Great in 550 BC and toppled by Alexander the Great in 330 BC; the Parthians, who threw off Seleucid rule in 247 BC and famously humbled Rome at Carrhae; and the Sasanians, who revived Persian imperial rule in 224 AD and held it until the Arab conquest of 651 AD.
imageAttribution: Map by Cattette, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Cyrus the Great Founds the Achaemenid Empire
events.body: Cyrus II defeats the Median Empire and unites the Medes and Persians under Achaemenid rule, founding what will become the largest empire the ancient world had yet seen.
events.imageAttribution: Photo by Surenae, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Cyrus Conquers Babylon, Frees the Jewish Captives
events.body: Cyrus captures Babylon and issues the Cyrus Cylinder, a declaration recording his restoration of displaced peoples and local temples — including freeing the Jewish captives held there since the Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem.
events.imageAttribution: Photo by Prioryman, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Construction Begins at Persepolis
events.body: Darius I begins building a new ceremonial capital in the Persian heartland, whose terraces, columned halls, and reliefs will showcase the empire's reach from Egypt to the Indus Valley.
events.imageAttribution: Photo by Alborzagros, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Battle of Thermopylae
events.body: Xerxes' invading army is delayed for three days at a narrow mountain pass by a small Greek force under the Spartan king Leonidas, whose stand becomes a lasting symbol of resistance even in defeat.
events.imageAttribution: Painting by Jacques-Louis David, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Achaemenid Empire Falls to Alexander the Great
events.body: Darius III, the last Achaemenid king, is killed by his own satraps while fleeing Alexander the Great's invasion, bringing the two-century-old empire to an end.
events.imageAttribution: Photo by Carole Raddato, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail of the Alexander Mosaic)

events.title: The Parthian Empire Is Founded
events.body: Arsaces I leads the Parni tribe in seizing the region of Parthia from the crumbling Seleucid Empire, founding a new Iranian dynasty that will rule for the next 470 years.
events.imageAttribution: Map by Ro4444 (edited), CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Battle of Carrhae
events.body: A Roman invasion force under Crassus is lured into open desert and destroyed by Parthian cavalry under the general Surena, in one of Rome's most catastrophic defeats.
events.imageAttribution: Theodore Ayrault Dodge, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Sasanian Dynasty Rises
events.body: Ardashir I defeats the last Parthian king and founds a new Persian empire under the House of Sasan, which will rival Rome and later Byzantium for over four centuries.
events.imageAttribution: Map by Ro4444 (edited), CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Shapur I Captures the Roman Emperor Valerian
events.body: Sasanian king Shapur I defeats a Roman army at Edessa and takes Emperor Valerian prisoner — the first time a reigning Roman emperor is ever captured in battle.
events.imageAttribution: Photo by Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Sasanian Empire Falls to Arab Conquest
events.body: After the Rashidun Caliphate's forces overrun the empire, the last Sasanian king, Yazdegerd III, is murdered while fleeing near Merv, and Persia is absorbed into the expanding Islamic caliphate.
events.imageAttribution: Map by Javierfv1212, edited by HistoryofIran, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Qin Shi Huang Unifies China
events.body: After conquering the last rival state, Ying Zheng declares himself First Emperor and standardizes script, currency, and roads across a unified China.

events.title: Construction Begins on the Great Wall
events.body: Existing frontier walls are joined and extended under Qin rule to defend against northern nomadic incursions.

events.title: Cai Lun Refines Papermaking
events.body: A court eunuch perfects a process for making paper from bark, hemp, and rags, transforming the spread of writing across Asia.

events.title: Tang Taizong Becomes ‘Heavenly Khan’
events.body: Steppe leaders acknowledge the Tang emperor as supreme ruler, opening a golden age of trade along the Silk Road.

events.title: Mongols Conquer the Song Dynasty
events.body: Kublai Khan's forces defeat the last Song loyalists at the Battle of Yamen, bringing all of China under Mongol Yuan rule for the first time.

events.title: The Classic Period Begins
events.body: Maya city-states like Tikal and Calakmul enter their peak era of monumental architecture, written history, and dynastic rivalry.

events.title: Teotihuacan's Influence Reaches Tikal
events.body: A political upheaval at Tikal, linked to contact with the distant central Mexican city of Teotihuacan, installs a new ruling dynasty.

events.title: Pakal Ascends the Throne at Palenque
events.body: Twelve-year-old K'inich Janaab' Pakal begins a 68-year reign that will make Palenque one of the Classic Period's greatest artistic centers.

events.title: Quiriguá Captures and Sacrifices Copán's King
events.body: Vassal city Quiriguá defeats its former overlord Copán in battle, upending the political order of the southeastern Maya lowlands.

events.title: The Last Long Count Date Is Carved
events.body: A monument at Toniná records the final Classic Maya calendar inscription, as southern lowland cities are abandoned in the following decades.

events.title: Constantinople Is Founded
events.body: Emperor Constantine dedicates a new capital on the Bosphorus, positioning the Eastern Roman Empire to outlast Rome itself by a thousand years.

events.title: Justinian's Code Is Compiled
events.body: A systematic codification of Roman law is issued, becoming the foundation of legal systems across continental Europe for centuries.

events.title: The Hagia Sophia Is Completed
events.body: Justinian's architects raise the largest cathedral in the world, its vast dome said to make the emperor exclaim he had surpassed Solomon.

events.title: The Great Schism Divides the Church
events.body: Theological and political disputes split Christianity into the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.

events.title: Constantinople Falls to the Ottomans
events.body: After a 53-day siege, Sultan Mehmed II's forces breach the city's ancient walls, ending the Byzantine Empire and the last direct link to Rome.

events.title: The Hijra Marks Year One
events.body: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina, an event that becomes the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: The Rashidun Caliphate Begins
events.body: Following Muhammad's death, a series of elected caliphs rapidly expand Muslim rule across Arabia, the Levant, and Persia.

events.title: The Abbasid Caliphate Is Founded
events.body: The Abbasids overthrow the Umayyads and move the capital to Baghdad, ushering in an Islamic Golden Age of science and scholarship.

events.title: The House of Wisdom Flourishes in Baghdad
events.body: Scholars translate and expand on Greek, Persian, and Indian texts, advancing mathematics, medicine, and astronomy.

events.title: The Mongols Sack Baghdad
events.body: Hulagu Khan's forces destroy the Abbasid capital and its libraries, an event many historians mark as the end of the Golden Age.

events.title: Jayavarman II Founds the Khmer Empire
events.body: A ruler declares himself universal monarch atop Phnom Kulen, unifying rival principalities into what will become the Khmer Empire.

events.title: Yasodharapura Becomes the Capital
events.body: King Yasovarman I establishes a new capital near Angkor, anchored by a temple-mountain dedicated to Shiva.

events.title: Construction of Angkor Wat Begins
events.body: Suryavarman II commissions the largest religious monument in the world, originally dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu.

events.title: A Chinese Envoy Records Daily Life
events.body: Zhou Daguan's detailed account of Angkor becomes one of the only surviving eyewitness descriptions of the empire at its height.

events.title: Ayutthaya Sacks Angkor
events.body: A Siamese army captures the capital after a prolonged siege, hastening the empire's shift of power away from Angkor.

events.title: Genghis Khan Unites the Mongol Tribes
events.body: A kurultai of chieftains proclaims Temüjin as Genghis Khan, “universal ruler,” beginning the fastest territorial expansion in history.

events.title: The Invasion of Khwarazm Begins
events.body: Genghis Khan turns west, destroying the Khwarazmian Empire in Central Asia in retaliation for the killing of Mongol envoys.

events.title: The Mongols Sack Baghdad
events.body: Hulagu Khan's western campaign topples the Abbasid Caliphate, extending Mongol power into the heart of the Islamic world.

events.title: Kublai Khan Founds the Yuan Dynasty
events.body: Genghis Khan's grandson declares a new Chinese dynasty, ruling as both Mongol Great Khan and Chinese emperor.

events.title: The Yuan Dynasty Falls
events.body: Ming rebels led by Zhu Yuanzhang drive the Mongols back to the steppe, ending nearly a century of Mongol rule over China.

events.title: Sundiata Keita Founds the Mali Empire
events.body: After defeating the sorcerer-king Sumanguru at Kirina, Sundiata unites the Mandinka clans into an empire that will control West Africa's gold trade.

events.title: Sakoura Expands Mali's Reach
events.body: A former palace slave seizes the throne and extends Mali's borders to the Atlantic coast and the Saharan salt mines.

events.title: Mansa Musa's Pilgrimage to Mecca
events.body: Mali's emperor travels to Mecca with a caravan reportedly carrying tons of gold, spending so freely in Cairo that he depresses regional gold prices for years.

events.title: Sankoré Madrasa Flourishes in Timbuktu
events.body: Timbuktu becomes a center of Islamic scholarship, drawing scholars and manuscripts from across the Muslim world.

events.title: Songhai Captures Timbuktu
events.body: Sunni Ali's Songhai forces seize Mali's great trading city, marking the empire's decline as Songhai rises in its place.

events.title: Tenochtitlan Is Founded
events.body: According to legend, the Mexica see an eagle perched on a cactus devouring a serpent — the sign they were seeking — and build their capital on a lake island.

events.title: The Triple Alliance Forms
events.body: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan unite, launching the rapid expansion that will become the Aztec Empire.

events.title: The Great Temple Is Dedicated
events.body: Tens of thousands are said to attend the consecration of the rebuilt Templo Mayor, marking the empire near the height of its power.

events.title: Cortés Arrives on the Coast
events.body: Hernán Cortés lands with a small Spanish force, soon allying with rivals of the Aztecs as he marches toward Tenochtitlan.

events.title: The Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.body: After a brutal siege and a smallpox epidemic that devastates the city, Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies capture the Aztec capital.

events.title: Pachacuti Begins the Inca Expansion
events.body: After repelling a rival invasion, Pachacuti reorganizes Cusco and launches the conquests that transform a small kingdom into an empire.

events.title: Machu Picchu Is Built
events.body: A royal estate rises high in the Andes, connected to the empire by a vast network of mountain roads and suspension bridges.

events.title: Atahualpa Is Captured at Cajamarca
events.body: Francisco Pizarro's small expedition ambushes the Inca emperor, despite being vastly outnumbered, exploiting a recent civil war and Spanish weaponry.

events.title: Atahualpa Is Executed
events.body: Despite paying a legendary ransom in gold and silver, the emperor is killed, and Spanish forces install a puppet ruler in Cusco.

events.title: The Last Inca Stronghold Falls
events.body: Spanish forces capture Vilcabamba and execute Túpac Amaru, ending organized Inca resistance four decades after first contact.
